source_text: Πᾶσα δόξα καὶ πλατυσμὸς ἐδόθη ὑμῖν, καὶ ἐπετελέσθη τὸ γεγραμμένον: Ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔπιεν, καὶ ἐπλατύνθη, καὶ ἐπαχύνθη, καὶ ἀπελάκτισεν ὁ ἠγαπημένος. ἐκ τούτου ζῆλος καὶ φθόνος, καὶ ἔρις, καὶ στάσις, διωγμὸς καὶ ἀκαταστασία, πόλεμος καὶ αἰχμαλωσία. οὕτως ἐπηγέρθησαν οἱ ἄτιμοι ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐντίμους, οἱ ἄδοξοι ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐνδόξους, οἱ ἄφρονες ἐπὶ τοὺς φρονίμους, οἱ νέοι ἐπὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους. διὰ τοῦτο πόρρω ἄπεστιν ἡ δικαιοσύνη καὶ εἰρήνη, ἐν τῷ ἀπολιπεῖν ἕκαστον τὸν φόβον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ πίστει αὐτοῦ ἀμβλυωπῆσαι, μηδὲ ἐν τοῖς νομίμοις τῶν προσταγμάτων αὐτοῦ πορεύεσθαι, μηδὲ πολιτεύεσθαι κατὰ τὸ καθῆκον τῷ Χριστῷ, ἀλλὰ ἕκαστον βαδίζειν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ τῆς πονηρᾶς, ζῆλον ἄδικον καὶ ἀσεβῆ ἀνειληφότας, δἰ οὖ καὶ θάνατος εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
pass_a_gloss: Every glory and enlargement was given to you, and the written thing was fulfilled: He ate and drank, and was enlarged, and was fattened, and the beloved kicked; from this zeal and envy, and strife, and faction, and persecution, and instability, war and captivity; thus the dishonored were raised up against the honored, the inglorious against the glorious, the foolish against the wise, the young against the elders; because of this righteousness and peace are far away, in each one leaving the fear of God and in His faith being dim-sighted, nor walking in the lawful things of His commands, nor living according to what is proper to Christ, but each one walking according to the desires of his own evil heart, having taken up unjust and impious zeal, through which also death entered into the world.

choices.why: translation of the verb in this context

pass_b_english: Every glory and expansion were given to you, and what was written was fulfilled: He ate and drank, grew large, grew fat, and the beloved kicked. From this came zeal and envy, strife and faction, persecution and instability, war and captivity. Thus the dishonored rose up against the honored, the inglorious against the glorious, the foolish against the wise, the young against the elders. Because of this, righteousness and peace are far off, since each one abandons the fear of God and grows dim-sighted in faith, neither walking in the lawful requirements of His commands nor living as befits Christ, but each one walking according to the desires of his own evil heart, having taken up unjust and impious zeal, through which death also entered the world.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'πολιτεύεσθαι' as 'living' or 'living as befits' is a valid semantic rendering of the concept of conducting one's life/citizenship in a certain manner. The translation of 'ἀμβλυωπῆσαι' as 'dim-sighted' is a faithful rendering of the verb.
